claims.text: Mn or Cu are ductility-enhancing elements for eutectic high-entropy alloys.
Adding Mn or Cu to a eutectic high-entropy alloy will increase its strength.
Adding Mn or Cu to a eutectic high-entropy alloy will increase its ductility.
The Mn or Cu addition alters the alloy microstructure.
The Mn or Cu addition produces a more favorable phase composition.
The Mn or Cu addition increases the volume fraction of a ductile phase.
Increasing the ductile-phase fraction enhances the alloy's overall ductility.
The proposed phase change maintains or increases strength while enhancing ductility.
The intervention will increase strength by at least 10% relative to the baseline alloy.
The intervention will increase ductility by at least 15% relative to the baseline alloy.
The alloy's microstructure and properties are optimized when Mn or Cu is added at 1–5 at.%.
The claimed effect should hold under standard casting followed by microstructure-optimizing heat treatment.
The baseline is an as-cast eutectic high-entropy alloy without Mn or Cu addition.
The exact ductility-enhancement mechanism may depend on alloy composition and processing conditions.
Tensile testing and microstructural analysis of modified and unmodified alloys can test the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The treated alloy is to be heat-treated, whereas the stated baseline is as-cast. Unless both modified and control alloys receive identical thermal processing, the comparison confounds elemental addition with heat treatment.

The prediction requires at least 10% greater strength and 15% greater ductility, but falsification is defined only when both improvements are below 5%. Outcomes between these thresholds, or failure of only one predicted property, are left non-decisive.
The requested single intervention is not uniquely specified: Mn and Cu are presented as alternatives, and the conditions also introduce heat treatment as an additional intervention.
